# `exemptions.exemption_tag` — version 1.0

Source: `presets/exemptions/exemption-tag.satz`

## Purpose

The vocabulary for a tag-conditional exemption: one organisation tag key with two
values, and nothing bound to either.

An org policy is all-or-nothing per node. To let ONE service account create ONE key,
the policy has to be lowered for a whole project or folder and raised again
afterwards — a lift WINDOW during which nothing is enforced and nobody remembers to
close it. A Resource Manager TAG replaces the window: unlike a label it is
IAM-governed and an org policy's rule can CONDITION on it, so the policy stays
enforced everywhere and named resources are let out one at a time.

Google does this themselves. Since 2024 a new organisation gets
`iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation` carrying
`resource.matchTagId('tagKeys/…', 'tagValues/…')` against a built-in key, so binding
`not_enforced` to one service account exempts that account and nothing else.

---- BEFORE granting any exemption, the question that usually ends it -------------

Does the consumer need a KEY at all? A workload inside Google Cloud, a Cloud Run
service, and external CI on GitHub or GitLab can all use Workload Identity Federation
or impersonation and leave the control intact. The tag route is the exception with a
named owner, never the default.

---- WHAT THIS PACK DOES AND DOES NOT DO -------------------------------------------

It ships the ABILITY, not the exemptions. A library that ships convenient exemptions
is a library that lowers the baseline by default. So: the key and the two values are
here; the BINDING that exempts a resource is the estate's, written where an auditor
reads it, and the policy CONDITION that honours the tag is written per constraint.

The binding, in the estate, one per exempted resource and each with a comment saying
who owns it and until when:

google_tags_tag_binding {
"svc-legacy-etl-key" {
// Owner: the platform team. Review: the next quarter's access review.
// Reason: the vendor's connector cannot federate; migration ticket OPS-1234.
parent    = "//iam.googleapis.com/projects/{infra_project_name}/serviceAccounts/…"
tag_value = "${{google_tags_tag_value.exemption_not_enforced.name}}"
}
}

The condition, on the constraint that should honour it — a second rule BEFORE the
unconditional one, turning enforcement off only where the value is bound:

rules = [
{
enforce = "FALSE"
condition {
title      = "exempted resources"
expression = "resource.matchTagId('${{google_tags_tag_key.exemption.name}}', '${{google_tags_tag_value.exemption_not_enforced.name}}')"
}
},
{ enforce = "TRUE" },
]

`require` reads that rule from the estate and prints it under the control
(`↳ exempted: …`) rather than letting a conditional policy read as plain "enforced";
`report-compliance` lists the live conditional rules beside the live verdict. The
org-wide answer to "who is exempted" is Cloud Asset Inventory:

gcloud asset search-all-resources --scope=organizations/ORG \
--query='tagValues:{customer_shortname}-exemption/not_enforced'

## Use it

```
params {
  use_exemption_tag = true
}

use "presets/exemptions/exemption-tag.satz" when use_exemption_tag
```

`use_exemption_tag` is the gate: while it is falsy the pack contributes nothing — no resources, no params, no claims. It is declared by `estate_map`, and the estate's own binding wins.

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `customer_organization_id` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `customer_shortname` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

_None — the pack takes everything from the estate's params._

An organisation policy is all-or-nothing per node, so letting one service account out of a control means lowering the policy for a whole folder and raising it again — a window during which nothing is enforced. A Resource Manager tag is IAM-governed and a policy rule can condition on it, which is how Google ships `iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation` themselves. The pack ships the ABILITY and no exemptions: a library that ships convenient exemptions lowers the baseline by default.
